paras: The killing of Felix Burke was the fatal shooting of a Black man by Deputy Sheriff McDonald in Monroe County, Arkansas, in early November 1881, while the deputy was trying to arrest him on a charge of stealing a mule. McDonald was badly wounded in the exchange of fire, and the episode reached distant newspapers only as a brief telegraphic crime item.

According to a Little Rock special relayed through Cincinnati, the man, whom that version called Felix Burell, was accused of having stolen a mule from a widow two months earlier and of returning to steal another.

When McDonald attempted the arrest, a "fierce pistol fight" broke out between the two men, in the Tribune's words, while the Omaha Bee's version described a "running fight." McDonald shot and killed the man and was himself "dangerously wounded," or "badly wounded" in the Bee's account. Neither report names a town or site within the county or says who fired first.
No report of an inquest, of McDonald's recovery or of any official inquiry appears in the coverage.

Both known reports came from Little Rock and ran in out-of-state crime columns among other short telegrams. The New-York Tribune printed its item on November 6 under the headline "Killed in Resisting a Sheriff," identifying the dead man as "a negro." The Omaha Daily Bee ran its version the next day as "A Mule Thief Killed," calling him "a mule thief" as a matter of fact and not mentioning his race. Both accounts rest on the officer's side of the encounter, and neither carries any statement from the dead man's family or community.

The two reports disagree on the man's surname, printed as Burke in the Tribune and Burell in the Bee. They also imply different dates: the Tribune's dispatch, dated Little Rock, November 5, placed the killing "yesterday," or November 4, while the Bee's Cincinnati dispatch of November 6 also said "yesterday," which would be November 5. The Tribune's direct Little Rock dateline makes November 4 the better-supported date.

Two differently worded Little Rock reports, one carried by the New-York Tribune and one relayed through Cincinnati to the Omaha Bee, agree that Deputy Sheriff McDonald killed the man in a gunfight in Monroe County and was himself badly wounded, though they spell the surname differently and may share an origin (A1, A2).

accounts.label: Little Rock dispatch (New-York Tribune)
accounts.gist: Felix Burke, 'a negro', was killed by Deputy Sheriff McDonald, who was trying to arrest him for stealing a mule; the two exchanged pistol fire and McDonald was dangerously wounded.

accounts.label: Little Rock special via Cincinnati (Omaha Bee)
accounts.gist: McDonald shot and killed Felix Burell, 'a mule thief', in a running fight and was badly wounded; Burell had allegedly stolen a widow's mule two months earlier and came back for another.

framing.detail: The Tribune ran the item as 'Killed in Resisting a Sheriff' among telegraphed crimes, giving the officer's attempted arrest as the setting and naming the man's race.
The Omaha Bee headlined 'A Mule Thief Killed' and called the dead man 'a mule thief' as fact, adding the earlier theft from a widow.
